Day 1
From Hotel: 🚶 9 min · 🚕 6 min → Hamburger Rathaus
1. Hamburger Rathaus
Neo-Renaissance city hall built 1886–1897 with 647 rooms and a 112 m tower; one of the few completely preserved historicist civic buildings in Germany. The open courtyard with its Hygieia fountain and the vaulted Rathausdiele foyer are freely accessible.
📖 Read more
🏛️ Monday - Sunday 8:00am - 6:00pm
⏰ ~1 hr
Free
📍 Rathausmarkt 1 · Altstadt
🚶 3 min · 🚕 2 min → Jungfernstieg & Binnenalster
2. Jungfernstieg & Binnenalster
Hamburg's grand 600 m boulevard along the southern shore of the Binnenalster lake — Germany's first asphalt-paved street, laid in 1838. The promenade gives a panoramic view of the Alster fountain and the city skyline reflected in the water.
📖 Read more
🏛️ Open 24/7
⏰ ~45 min
📍 Jungfernstieg · Neustadt
🚶 9 min · 🚕 6 min → St. Nikolai Memorial
3. St. Nikolai Memorial
The bombed-out shell of the neo-Gothic St. Nikolai church, kept as a memorial to the victims of war. Its 147 m spire was briefly the tallest building in the world; a glass lift climbs to a 76 m viewing platform, with an exhibition on the 1943 air raids in the crypt.
📖 Read more
St. Nikolai Memorial · 4.5⭐ · mahnmal-st-nikolai.de
🏛️ Daily 10:00am - 6:00pm
⏰ ~45 min
📍 Willy-Brandt-Straße 60 · Altstadt
🚶 10 min · 🚕 5 min → Chilehaus
4. Chilehaus
A ten-story Brick Expressionist office building designed by Fritz Höger in 1924, whose two facades meet at an impossibly sharp angle like the prow of a ship. Part of the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Kontorhaus District — the world's first purpose-built office quarter.
📖 Read more
🏛️ Open 24/7
⏰ ~30 min
📍 Fischertwiete 2 · Altstadt
🚶 5 min · 🚕 3 min → hotel
Day 2
From Hotel: 🚶 26 min · 🚕 7 min → Planten un Blomen
1. Planten un Blomen
A 47-hectare inner-city park whose name is Low German for "plants and flowers." It holds Europe's largest Japanese garden with a teahouse, tropical greenhouses, and a lake with water-light concerts in summer evenings.
📖 Read more
🏛️ Daily 7:00am - 11:00pm
⏰ ~1 hr 30 min
Free
📍 Holstenwall 8 · Neustadt
🚶 9 min · 🚕 2 min → St. Michaelis Church Tower
2. St. Michaelis Church Tower
Hamburg's most iconic landmark — the largest Protestant baroque church in northern Germany. Its 132 m copper-roofed tower offers a 360° viewing platform at 106 m reached by lift or 452 steps, overlooking the harbour, Elbe, and city centre.
📖 Read more
St. Michaelis Tower · 4.5⭐ · st-michaelis.de
🏛️ Daily 10:00am - 6:00pm
⏰ ~1 hr
📍 Englische Planke 1 · Neustadt
🚶 8 min · 🚕 4 min → Alter Elbtunnel
3. Alter Elbtunnel
A 426 m pedestrian tunnel running 24 m beneath the Elbe, opened in 1911 — an engineering marvel of its era with original Art Nouveau tilework and terracotta reliefs of fish and marine life. The south exit offers a panoramic view back toward the Hamburg skyline.
📖 Read more
🏛️ Open 24/7
⏰ ~30 min
📍 St. Pauli-Landungsbrücken 7 · St. Pauli
🚶 17 min · 🚕 6 min → Elbphilharmonie
4. Elbphilharmonie
Herzog & de Meuron's concert hall, a glass-and-steel wave set on a 1960s brick warehouse on the Elbe. The free public Plaza wraps the building at 37 m for a 360° view of the harbour and city; timed Plaza tickets are issued at the visitor centre.
📖 Read more
🏛️ Daily 10:00am - 11:30pm
⏰ ~1 hr
Free
📍 Platz der Deutschen Einheit 1 · HafenCity
🚶 28 min · 🚕 6 min → hotel
Day 3
From Hotel: 🚶 31 min · 🚕 7 min → Landungsbrücken
1. Landungsbrücken
Hamburg's 700 m historic floating dock and waterfront terminal, built 1907–1909 and flanked by two green-domed towers. The elevated walkway above the S-Bahn station gives a sweeping panorama over the Elbe, harbour cranes, and passing container ships.
📖 Read more
🏛️ Open 24/7
⏰ ~30 min
📍 Bei den St. Pauli-Landungsbrücken · St. Pauli
🚶 17 min · 🚕 3 min → Miniatur Wunderland
2. Miniatur Wunderland
The world's largest model railway, spread across themed miniature worlds — Hamburg, the Alps, Scandinavia, the USA and a working model airport — with thousands of trains, vehicles, ships and aircraft in motion. Germany's most-visited attraction.
📖 Read more
Miniatur Wunderland · 4.7⭐ · miniatur-wunderland.com
🏛️ Daily 9:30am - 6:00pm
⏰ ~2 hr
📍 Kehrwieder 2 · Speicherstadt
🚶 11 min · 🚕 4 min → Speicherstadt
3. Speicherstadt
The world's largest contiguous warehouse district, built on oak piles from 1883 and UNESCO-listed since 2015. Red-brick neo-Gothic storehouses line the tidal canals; the Wasserschloss on the Poggenmühlen bridge is its most-photographed view.
📖 Read more
🏛️ Open 24/7
⏰ ~45 min
📍 Poggenmühlenbrücke · Speicherstadt
🚕 22 min → Blankenese Treppenviertel
4. Blankenese Treppenviertel
A 700-year-old former fishing village with 58 staircases comprising nearly 5,000 steps winding around the 72 m Süllberg hill. Mediterranean-feeling white houses, hidden gardens, and panoramic Elbe views at every turn — unlike anything else in a northern European city.
📖 Read more
🏛️ Open 24/7
⏰ ~2 hr
📍 Treppenviertel · Blankenese
🚕 25 min → hotel
Day 4
From Hotel: 🚶 8 min · 🚕 6 min → Hamburger Kunsthalle
1. Hamburger Kunsthalle
One of Germany's largest art museums, housed in three linked buildings from 1869, 1921 and 1997. The collection spans 700 years of European art, from medieval altarpieces to contemporary work — including Friedrich's Wanderer above the Sea of Fog, works by Rembrandt, Manet and Picasso.
📖 Read more
Hamburger Kunsthalle · 4.6⭐ · hamburger-kunsthalle.de
🏛️ Tuesday - Wednesday 10:00am - 6:00pm · Thursday 10:00am - 9:00pm · Friday - Sunday 10:00am - 6:00pm
🚫 Closed Monday
⏰ ~2 hr
📍 Glockengießerwall 5 · Altstadt
🚶 8 min · 🚕 3 min → Außenalster
2. Außenalster
Hamburg's vast outer Alster lake, 1.6 km long and ringed by a 7.5 km promenade of 19th-century villas, parkland and sailing clubs. The western shore along Harvestehuder Weg offers the city's most celebrated skyline panorama — steeples of the Altstadt and Elbphilharmonie reflected across open water.
📖 Read more
🏛️ Open 24/7
⏰ ~45 min
📍 Harvestehuder Weg · Harvestehude
🚕 12 min → Reeperbahn
3. Reeperbahn
Hamburg's 930 m entertainment quarter in St. Pauli — Germany's most internationally famous street. The Beatles honed their craft here in 1960–62, playing marathon sets at the Indra and Kaiserkeller clubs before the Star-Club became their Hamburg home. Today it's a strip of theatres, clubs and music venues.
📖 Read more
🏛️ Open 24/7
⏰ ~30 min
📍 Reeperbahn 1 · St. Pauli
🚶 2 min · 🚕 2 min → Beatles-Platz
4. Beatles-Platz
A circular plaza at Reeperbahn and Große Freiheit, its black pavement designed to resemble a vinyl record. Five steel silhouettes on tall poles represent John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison, Stuart Sutcliffe and Pete Best — marking where the Fab Four played from 1960 to 1962.
📖 Read more
🏛️ Open 24/7
⏰ ~20 min
📍 Beatles-Platz · St. Pauli
🚶 40 min · 🚕 10 min → hotel

🍮 Local Tastes
Franzbrötchen
A buttery, cinnamon-sugar laminated pastry pressed flat in the middle — Hamburg's signature sweet, eaten for breakfast or as a snack.
📍 Mutterland · Schmidt & Schmidtchen
Fischbrötchen
A bread roll filled with North Sea shrimp, matjes or Bismarck herring, fried Backfisch or smoked salmon, with onions and remoulade — classic harbour street food.
📍 Brücke 10 · Daniel Wischer
Labskaus
A sailor's hash of corned beef, potato and beetroot mashed pink, served with a fried egg, gherkins and rollmops or Bismarck herring.
📍 Old Commercial Room · Krameramtsstuben
Pannfisch
Pan-fried fish fillets in mustard sauce with sautéed potatoes — a Hanseatic classic that began as a way to use up leftover fish.
📍 Krameramtsstuben · Deichgraf
Finkenwerder Scholle
Plaice fried Finkenwerder-style with diced bacon and North Sea shrimp, named after the Elbe island of Finkenwerder — a spring favourite.
📍 Fischereihafen Restaurant
Rote Grütze
A thick red-berry compote of redcurrants, raspberries and cherries cooked to a set pudding, served with vanilla sauce, cream or ice cream.
📍 Old Commercial Room

⛲️ Day Trips by Train
Lüneburg · 30 min
A well-preserved medieval salt-trading town of crooked gabled houses, brick architecture and an old harbour quarter — the quickest of these trips to reach.
🎫 book at: Deutsche Bahn or Omio
Lübeck · 45 min
A UNESCO-listed Hanseatic old town on an island, entered through the medieval Holstentor gate — famous for its brick Gothic churches and marzipan.
🎫 book at: Deutsche Bahn or Omio
Bremen · 1 hr
A Hanseatic city with a UNESCO-listed Marktplatz, the Town Hall and Roland statue, the Town Musicians of Bremen sculpture, and the medieval Schnoor lane quarter.
🎫 book at: Deutsche Bahn or Omio
Schwerin · 1 hr
Capital of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, where the fairytale Schweriner Schloss sits on its own island in Lake Schwerin, ringed by a well-preserved center and a chain of lakes.
🎫 book at: Deutsche Bahn or Omio
Stade · 1 hr
A historic Hanseatic port town with a well-preserved old town of half-timbered houses, the Alter Hansehafen and the Schwedenspeicher museum.
🎫 book at: Deutsche Bahn or Omio

✨ Worth Knowing

Notes from the Harbour City

Hamburg has more bridges than Venice, Amsterdam and London combined — over 2,500 of them — a consequence of building a port across the marshy islands where the Alster meets the Elbe. Almost every walk in the old centre crosses water.

Four days trace the city's whole arc. Day 1 follows the waterfront from the 2017 Elbphilharmonie through the 1880s Speicherstadt to the 1943 ruin of St. Nikolai — port wealth, war, and reinvention stacked along one mile of the Elbe. Day 2 pulls back to the civic core: the Rathaus with its 647 rooms, the Alster lake that makes Hamburg feel more like a Scandinavian capital than a German port, and the Michel tower that has marked the city's skyline since 1786. Day 3 descends to the working harbour and the Elbe tunnel that runs beneath it, then reaches the fishing-village staircases of Blankenese — proof that Hamburg's edges are as surprising as its centre. Day 4 crosses the cultural divide: the Kunsthalle's seven centuries of European art, the enormous quiet of the Außenalster lake ringed by sailing clubs, and then west to St. Pauli — to the Reeperbahn and the circular plaza where the Beatles' Hamburg story is marked in steel.
